issues.title: Custom resource pack death sounds play briefly then cut off after player death
issues.body:
### Bug description

When using a resource pack with custom, longer death sound effects (such as the Excalibur resource pack: https://modrinth.com/resourcepack/excal), the sound starts playing normally for a few seconds upon death, but then abruptly cuts off before finishing. The audio thread seems to be dropped or forcefully culled mid-way through. 

Disabling the Sound Physics Remastered mod completely resolves the issue, allowing the full death audio to finish seamlessly.

### Minecraft version

1.21.1

### Mod version

neoforge-1.21.1-1.4.10

### Mod loader and version

NeoForge (Minecraft 1.21.1)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Equip the Excalibur resource pack (https://modrinth.com/resourcepack/excal).
2. Ensure Sound Physics Remastered is enabled on a NeoForge instance.
3. Die in-game.
4. Observe the custom audio playing normally for a few seconds before abruptly cutting off as the death screen stays up.

### Expected behavior

The full custom audio track from the resource pack should continue playing to completion instead of being cut off early.

### Log files

No crash log generated as this is a pure audio playback culling glitch.

### Videos

https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1553779425877696615/1553811675294208160/Minecraft_NeoForge__1.21.1_-_Singleplayer_2026-09-27_23-47-03.mp4?ex=6abb4423&is=6ab9f2a3&hm=d1c488e3822f2ecaa3bc0f0ea3d8bed42ec91cf844999c3180bbc55e952317cf&

issues.title: Severe FPS drops with many entities in a confined area
issues.body: ### Bug description **- Description:** Sound Physics Remastered causes severe and disproportionate FPS drops when there are many entities in a confined area. This is particularly noticeable when there is a solid barrier between the player and the entities. In a fresh Superflat world with spawning gamerules disabled, having a lot of entities near the entity cap per block (e.g. villagers) confined to a small area (e.g. 5x5) can cause the FPS to drop from a stable locked 160 FPS to around 2 FPS when the entities are behind a wall. When looking directly at the entities, the performance impact is much smaller: approximately from 160 FPS to 144 FPS. The issue disappears completely when Sound Physics Remastered is disabled, with the game returning to a stable 160 FPS under the same conditions. **- Actual behavior:** Sound Physics Remastered causes an extreme FPS drop when multiple entities are present in a confined area, with the worst performance occurring when a barrier blocks direct line of sight between the player and the entities. The behavior is highly reproducible and occurs even with a clean installation containing only the required Fabric components and Sound Physics Remastered. **- Additional observations:** I also tested the same scenario with Presence Footsteps. It appears to exhibit a similar performance issue when approaching areas containing many entities. When I turn Sound Physics Remastered off, the FPS returns to stable 160 FPS. So it's reproducible with any sound mod. However, my primary test was performed without Presence Footsteps, and the issue with Sound Physics Remastered remains fully reproducible. This makes me suspect that the issue may be related to the processing of a large number of simultaneous sound sources or sound simulations generated by entities. It would be useful if Sound Physics Remastered could provide an option to disable or limit sound simulation originating from entities (I know there are ways to limit it and i've tried it, but it breaks the whole mod experience, since it applies to other sound sources, and it doesn't really solve the FPS drop that much), similar to how Presence Footsteps provides control over its own sound sources. **- Test environment:** Java: Temurin JDK 25.0.4.1+1 OS: Windows 11 Pro JVM arguments: -Xms12G -Xmx12G -XX:+UseZGC -XX:+UseCompactObjectHeaders Launcher: ATLauncher **- Hardware:** CPU: Ryzen 7 5800X3D 10th Anniversary Edition GPU: RTX A2000 6 GB RAM: 32 GB DDR4-3200 CL16 (2×16 GB) Motherboard: ASUS TUF GAMING B550M-PLUS Storage: WD Green SN3000 2 TB Monitor: ASUS TUF Gaming VG249Q1R — 1920×1080 @ 165 Hz PSU: Montech Century II 850 W CPU cooler: Thermalright Peerless Assassin 120 SE V2 with Carbice Ice Pad **- Mods:** Sound Physics Remastered 1.5.1+26.3 Fabric API 0.161.0+26.3 Cloth Config 26.3.158 Mod Menu 21.0.0-beta.1 Presence Footsteps 1.14.0+26.3¹ ¹: For the primary reproduction, Presence Footsteps was disabled. ### Minecraft version 26.3 ### Mod version 1.14.0+26.3 ### Mod loader and version Fabric Loader 0.19.5 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a new Superflat world with mob spawning disabled. 2. Create a small confined area, such as a 5×5 hole. 3. Fill the area with villagers or other entities, enough to reach the mob cap. 4. Stand nearby and look directly at the entities. - FPS should drop only slightly (approximately from 160 to 144 FPS in my case). 5. Get behind a solid barrier between the player and the entities so that they are no longer directly visible. 6. Observe the FPS. - In my case, FPS drops dramatically from a stable 160 FPS to approximately 2 FPS. ### Expected behavior The presence of multiple entities should not cause such a severe performance impact, especially when the entities are not directly visible to the player (maybe add some sort of culling or default limit, though it might interfere with the purpose of the mod experience). Or just add a toggle button for entities interaction sounds. ### Log files https://gist.github.com/Prismie/42d8751c45ff86d97ca8b826e13b9bac ### Videos Looking Directly (SPR ON): Behind Wall (SPR ON): Looking Directly (SPR OFF): Behind Wall (SPR OFF): I couldn't make a video, but there are the prints. I didn't enable the debug rays since it'd affect the performance and therefore the expected proof of the bug.

issues.title: Latest 26.1 builds don't support 26.1
issues.body:
### Bug description

The latest builds for 26.1, built for 26.1.1, don't support 26.1.  
This is because the versions in `fabric.mod.json` are minimum not current.  
You have to specify the minimum Minecraft, Fabric Loader, etc versions in that file, not pass through the current versions used for compiling, because Fabric enforces the minimum versions listed in that file during runtime, even though the mod works fine otherwise.

I know from testing that the minimum fabric loader version that supports 26.1 is 0.16.14, but 0.17+ would also be a sensible choice.

Minecraft should be `>=26.1` not `~26.1.1` or `~26.1`

issues.title: Limit performance impact with a lot of sound sources
issues.body: ### Bug description This is not a bug, but there was no location to submitt improvement ideas. In an environment with a lot of sound sources (animals in farms, create factories or so) the calculations for the sound physics can tank the performance to single digits. That is expected as there is a loooooot to calculate, but for a normal player to understand why and disable the mod / change its config goes a long way. They usualy think its someting visual rendering and not the sound. Implementing a safeguard that disables the mod when a set of sound sources is reached (configurable by user) or it drops below a certain fps threshold would greatly improve the handling of such stress cases. ### Minecraft version 1.21.1 ### Mod version 1.21.1-1.5.1 ### Mod loader and version NeoForge 21.1.217 ### Steps to reproduce Enable the Mod, go near a Farm with a looooot of animas or other sound sources. or play rush_e on instruments see your fps go down ### Expected behavior the behavior is expected with that many sources, but a better behavior would be to disable the the calculations once a sound source threshold is reached or fps drop below a certain level ### Log files No Logs needed ### Videos We simulated the sound sources with immersive melodies, but any larger animal farm will result in the same. Here are some screens of the fps going down the more sound sources are playing

issues.title: Unsafe access of config in mixin causing you to be blamed for mod loading errors
issues.body:
### Bug description

In your mixin to SoundEgnine (loadLibrary) you attempt to access your config file. However, if another mod causes a mod loading error earlier on, (neo)forge will cowardly refuse to send events, including ones used to load configs, causing your config instance to be null.

You should do a null check and gracefully cancel loading if your config is null, as that indicates that (neo)forge is attempting to limp towards an error screen.


Example of the error that sound physics throws:
```
Error starting SoundSystem. Turning off sounds & music
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot read field "debugLogging" because "com.sonicether.soundphysics.SoundPhysicsMod.CONFIG" is null
	at com.sonicether.soundphysics.Loggers.logDebug(Loggers.java:38) ~[sound-physics-remastered-forge-1.20.1-1.4.10.jar%23406!/:1.20.1-1.4.10]

	at net.minecraft.client.sounds.SoundEngine.handler$dke000$loadLibrary(SoundEngine.java:589) ~[client-1.20.1-20230612.114412-srg.jar%23432!/:?]
```

### Minecraft version

Observed on 1.20.1, however code analysis shows this would still happen in current master branch

## Latest guess: Occlusion overrides the reflection sound if too many blocks are involved in occllusion, as seen in the videos below. (Reccomended to watch other videos listed in the bottom for context)

In the `evaluateEnvironment` function, the reflected rays (reflection) and occlusion rays (occlusion) are processed in parallel, but the final values (sendGain, sendCutoff, directGain and directCutoff) can be adjusted so that the reflected sound is "muffled" by occlusion.

In particular, the `directCutoff` variable and its associated values may be reduced too much due to high occlusion, even if there is a reflected path.

I'm getting a consistent crash when launching Minecraft 1.20.1 with Forge 47.3.0 on Linux (Nobara 41). The game crashes with a SIGFPE (divide-by-zero) in libopenal.so during startup. issues.title: 1.20.2/1.20.3 Update Blocker
issues.body:
In Minecraft 1.20.2 Mojang updated [LWJGL](https://github.com/LWJGL/lwjgl3) from [3.3.1](https://github.com/LWJGL/lwjgl3/releases/tag/3.3.1) to [3.3.2](https://github.com/LWJGL/lwjgl3/releases/tag/3.3.2).
This LWJGL update switched from [OpenAL Soft](https://github.com/kcat/openal-soft) from [1.21.1](https://github.com/kcat/openal-soft/blob/master/ChangeLog) to [1.23.0](https://github.com/kcat/openal-soft/blob/master/ChangeLog).

These changes seem to have introduced a bug in OpenAL Soft that causes the Sound Physics Mod to not have any reverb.

**This blocks the mod from getting updated to 1.20.2 or later!**

I would appreciate any help identifying the actual issue with OpenAL Soft/LWJGL.
If anyone has a workaround for that issue in the current Minecraft version, help is also really appreciated!

---

If you really want to use the mod on 1.20.2, you can use the [Prism Launcher](https://prismlauncher.org/) and change the LWJGL version back to 3.3.1.

![image](https://github.com/henkelmax/sound-physics-remastered/assets/13237524/443bff8b-0372-40dc-ae0d-4d8e5150b785)

issues.title: Valkyrie Skies Issues
issues.body:
**Bug description**
Crashes the Game When in use with Valkyrie Skies under special circumstances.

**Steps to reproduce the issue**
1. Install ValkyrieSkies with Eureka and install Waystones + this mod.
2. Place a waystone at spawn.
3. Fly 60 chunks away (If you load the chunk you teleport to sometimes it survives the crash)
4. Now build a really small eureka vessel, assemble it and add a waystone on it.
![image](https://github.com/henkelmax/sound-physics-remastered/assets/68244453/6902a25c-d382-4383-890b-3d467e02998a)

5. Go back to the waystone at the spawn and wait there 10 seconds to let the game unload the chunks.
6. Now teleport to it and crash

**Expected behavior**
That you can use the Waystone on the ship (It worked for me aslong as i had sound disabled)

**Log files**
[Logs](https://gist.github.com/Autumnlight02/065add1c7bf33a80d4604fb9e9164560)

--------------------------- **Why Does This happen?** ---------------------------
Valkyrie Skies Is an new upcomming amazing engine Which allows you to build ships and fully interact with them.
The way it works is as following:
When you assemble your Ship it basically duplicates all blocks on the world border. And then sends you a mirror, with which you can fully interact (chest block placing etc) And it feels like having a secondary coordinate system in minecraft)
Basically When you do an interaction like using a Waystone, You teleport to the world border, But that mod detect that teleport and automatically adjust your teleport to your new position (where the ship is). That works great with all kinds of mods. (besides this one).

So My assumption is that the sounds are likely too far away and that its confusing this mod, or that the chunks where the sounds play are not loaded and that causes the crash. 

--------------------------- **Possible fix?** ---------------------------
I could assume a possible fix would be to not play sounds out of bounds (The teleportation is so fast that it wont even render a frame). Or to introduce a special patch if valkyrie is installed

**Versions**
- Minecraft version : 1.18.2 - 40.2.10 && 40.2.7 (tested both)
- Forge/Fabric loader version: Forge 40.2.10
- Mod version : soundphysics-forge-1.18.2-1.0.6.jar

issues.title: Longer sounds aren't processed correctly
issues.body:
I'm making a map that requires a custom resource pack, and several of the new sounds I loaded into the game are rather long, ranging from several seconds of continuous sound to multiple minutes of machine room ambience. A problem I noticed with Sound Physics Remastered while constructing a submarine-like structure (that the player must navigate while PA loudspeakers dispatch messages and alarms blare) is that the reverb and suppression of the sounds appears to only process once. The issue is constant through several versions and both Forge and Fabric.

For example, when I use the `/playsound` command to start running a background drone of machinery in the engine room WHILE the character stands in the engine room as well, the sound is very clearly heard from anywhere within the structure, even through three stories of multilayered flooring and vessel decoration (copper and deepslate, to be specific). On the other hand, using `/playsound` while on the top floor of the build and the same play coordinates as the last test yields a nearly inaudible highly muffed and deepened version of the same sound. Even after walking down to the engine room and standing right next to the point where the sound is emitted, the initial result is unchanged. By the way, the ambience OGG file lasts about three minutes at normal pitch and speed.

Another example would be the PA announcements I mentioned; German and English warning audios repeated by a TTS robot inform the player of mechanical problems. In the event the player is next to one of the "speakers" (custom heads) when the audio is relayed, they'll be able to hear the entire message just fine throughout the whole building, but if it's repeated while the player happens to be in the ladder well or just behind a wall from a speaker, the sound will be totally muffled from any point in the build for the rest of the dispatch even if the player proceeds to run their face into the nearest PA speaker after the sound starts playing.

**TL;DR:** Long sounds are processed only once and remain at their initial play volume/pitch for the entire duration of the OGG file.

A system of repeated updates to the sound's position (similar to how Optifine tracks dynamic lighting) and its reverb waves would provide long sounds a more fluid playback as you move around them (e.g., the sound starts muffled behind a wall then grows clear once you step into its room).

issues.title: Sound Physics Remastered: Moving Forward
issues.body:
It's time to face the truth: Sound Physics Remastered is an obsolete fork of an older version of Sound Physics. Since it was released, all of the features and bugfixes have been implemented in the base mod in one form or another, along with many new features that were never in the remastered version. In addition, Sound Physics Remastered is barely maintained past updating to 1.18 and fixing bugs, whereas Sound Physics is actively maintained and I am developing new features constantly. Sound Physics Remastered had a good run as a great fork of the mod, but it's time that it stepped out of the spotlight and let the newer features take their place

I'm not proposing that Sound Physics Remastered be removed entirely, only that the fabric version is removed. I never plan to port to Forge, so I don't mind if you maintain a Forge port of the mod. All i ask is that you link to the fabric version in your mod description, and I will link to your page as the forge version. That way, we don't lose users when they realize that you no longer provide a fabric version.

I considered somehow keeping the fabric version of this fork, but I quickly realized that no matter what else I did, it would continue to take away from the work i have put into this mod. I also considered the complete removal of Sound Physics Remastered, but I do recognize the fact that you did put a lot of work into this mod originally, and I think you deserve some credit for that, so I decided it was best that you continue to provide the forge version.

I believe this is a good compromise that gets us both something that we are happy with, If i am wrong in thinking that, or if you would like to change some of the terms of the arrangement, just let me know. Otherwise, say the word and I will hold up my end of the agreement.

issues.title: What is your favourite config?
Implementation of Delay/Echo and Doppler effect
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
not really a problem beyond having reverb but no delay, because it's something you'd expect within the new caves and cliffs (literally) generation. doppler effect would just be an "attention to detail" feature of a more situational nature, so it not being there wouldn't make a big difference

**Describe the solution you'd like**
just as the mod currently makes reverb with material specific sound absorption levels, delay would be more or less noticeable depending on the material of the surroundings as well as how open the space is.
tbh Doppler sounds like it'd be more complex to achieve. it'd take into account the player's POV, and sound sources' position/momentum/velocity, then calculate and pitch up or down the sound accordingly. The most common occurrence of this would be while riding a minecart or horse, hearing a minecart pass by, flying with elytra, during a big fall (imagine a player's scream as they fall having the doppler effect, remember Mario Kart 64 characters screaming when they're hit and then they fall behind? especially in tunnels that even add delay?).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
i realise i don't know how Doppler would work with Simple Voice Chat specifically because it involves changing pitch, i can't imagine how it would apply to audio that comes and goes through the internet in real time, but since the effects the mode currently has are compatible with it i think it's probably feasible, if not then it's ok either way. On the other hand, while i think Echo sounds easier to add, it might be inconvenient for some people in Simple Voice Chat so a toggle for it could be needed

**Additional context**
for help on a good analysis on the Doppler effect in a videogame and how it's calculated, i know of [this video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lz5yiVBtPvs)
